title: OpenStax says a single early word can ask for something, not only name it
summary: OpenStax says a one-word utterance often carries a larger meaning, so cookie can name a cookie or ask for one.
body: OpenStax Psychology 7.2 says that in the one-word stage children know a number of words but produce only one-word utterances, and that these words often carry a larger meaning. The example is a child saying cookie, which could be identifying a cookie or asking for a cookie. The textbook cites Fernandez and Cairns, 2011. The example is an illustration in a CC BY 4.0 chapter, not a transcript of a particular child and not a CDC milestone.

sources.title: Psychology, section 7.2 Language

sources.note: First-edition web view at /books/psychology/, which the preface licenses CC BY 4.0. Opened 2026-11-26. No review date was printed on the section, so the source date is the access date. Paraphrase, with credit to OpenStax Psychology. Supports the cookie example: a one-word utterance can identify the thing or ask for it.
